title: Two Oil Tankers Freed From Pirates Off the Coast of Somalia
author: Mohamed Gabobe
content:
MOGADISHU, Somalia--The maritime force for Somalia's semi-autonomous Puntland
region has seized control of two separate hijacked oil tankers, Puntland
security sources tell Drop Site News.

Honour 25, which was hijacked by Somali pirates in late April was initially
carrying 18,500 barrels of oil (worth an estimated $1.7 million), while MT
Eureka seized in May was initially carrying 20,400 barrels of diesel (worth an
estimated $4.3 million).

The Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF)--created in 2013 with funding from
the United Arab Emirates and trained by private South African security firm
Saransor--is tasked with maritime security and anti-piracy operations in
Somali territorial waters that fall under Puntland's jurisdiction.

A statement released today by the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) stated
that, when it regained "control" of Honour 25, five members of the crew had
been killed--deaths they attributed to pirates--and four wounded during the
operation. The rest of the crew was rescued safely.

Multiple Puntland security officials interviewed today by Drop Site in the
hours following the rescue of Honour 25 say the decision to carry out
'attacks' on the hijacked vessels was made on September 9th, when following
weeks of surveillance, Puntland security officials had confirmed that pirates
on-board Honour 25 and MT Eureka had been offloading barrels of oil and diesel
from the hijacked vessels to shore.

"The pirates had been loading the barrels (of fuel) on to small boats, then
transporting them to shore," a Puntland security official told Drop Site.

"Once they moved the barrels (of fuel) to shore, their on-land criminal
network would take the barrels and sell them on the black market to local fuel
importers," a second Puntland official confirmed.

When asked for insight into the local fuel importers receiving the hijacked
barrels of fuel from the pirates on both ships, the Puntland security
officials declined to further comment, citing sensitivities around the ongoing
investigation. "They where trying to make two profits. Sell the fuel worth
millions, and also get a ransom for the hijacked ships and their crew," a
third Puntland security official told Drop Site.

**READ MORE:[Somali Pirates Demand $10M Ransom for Oil Tanker Owned by Emirati
Company](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/somali-pirates-demand-10-million-
dollar-ransom-oil-tanker-uae)**

Drones belonging to the European Union Naval Force (EUNAVFOR) provided
extensive surveillance ahead of the operation, officials said. EUNAVFOR is
tasked with anti-piracy operations in Somali territorial waters and had been
carrying out regular reconnaissance missions on both hijacked oil tankers.

Earlier on Tuesday, Puntland carried out the operation as it anchored near the
fishing settlement of Dbarin-baar using assets both in the air and at sea,
with Puntland officials declining to go into further detail due to what they
deemed as "operational security."

Puntland security officials tell us during the raid on Honour 25, 15 pirates
were captured, including an English-speaking translator who was leading
negotiations on the hijacked oil tanker. "When our men (troops) boarded the
ship, the interpreter didn't resist because he was unarmed," a second Puntland
security tells Drop Site.

"The bullet-riddled bodies of 5 foreign nationals was also on the ship (oil
tanker)," the second Puntland security official added. They were from
Pakistan, Burma, and India.

Once the raid on Honour 25 was underway, officials said, pirates on board MT
Eureka began setting the oil tanker on fire, then set off on small boats, with
the crew to shore.

These boats were anchored near MT Eureka and used by the pirates to move both
gunmen and supplies to and from shore, Puntland security officials said.
"After they set the ship (MT Eureka) ablaze, they took the crew at gunpoint
onto small boats and made their way to the fishing settlement of Hol-Caanood,"
a Puntland security official tells Drop Site.

MT Eureka, had 12 hostages on board, hailing from Egypt and India. "When the
pirates made it to Hol-Caanood, they handed over the crew to local residents
and continued fleeing," the Puntland security official says.

All three Puntland security officials interviewed by Drop Site news say around
30 gunmen (pirates) made it back to shore with their weapons and are currently
being pursued by the authorities.

Honour 25 is owned by a Somali businessman and MT Eureka is owned by a UAE-
based company called Royal Shipping Lines Inc. These latest incidents come
just a week after Puntland state [freed](https://mwanzotv.com/us-sanctioned-
oil-tanker-rescued-from-somali-pirates-puntland-officials/) Sibu-1, a
U.S.-sanctioned oil tanker with ties to Iran, in an operation off the coast of
Somalia. That operation came under intense scrutiny within the security
apparatus of Puntland after 28 captured pirates
[escaped](https://www.newarab.com/news/somali-pirates-escape-suspected-police-
help) during an armed police custody the following day.

One hijacked vessel, MT Asana, remains in the hands of pirates.
